summary: Design: sketch editing moves from the relations panel to the canvas, a thin bar and the feature tree. While a sketch is edited, a thin bar centred across the top of the view shows its name, its constraint status, a count of constraint issues that opens the list of conflicting, redundant or unmet relations and of curves a Symmetric solve shrank, the Show dimensions and Show relations toggles, a slot for view modes, Finish and, for a sketch a solid uses, Cancel sketch edits. In Select, a selection of points and edges shows a row of relation icons beside it, built from the relation registry's offers for that selection without a solve. The row is placed clear of the selected points and edges themselves and, where it can, of dimension labels, relation marks, floating panels and the bar; when no place is clear it stays hidden and the status line points to the Constrain menu and the Dimension tool. Available relations press to apply, applied ones show pressed and press to remove the relations they name, and blocked ones are disabled and say why. Every press goes through the same native check as any relation edit, so a conflicting relation is refused, the part keeps its version and the bar counts the conflict. The row covers selections of several elements, Fix for points, Symmetric, Symmetric centers for two circles and a line or axis, Concentric and Tangent, and ends with Dimension the selection, which starts the Dimension tool on the picks. It hides while drawing or dragging; while an edit applies it stays in place but inactive, so the pressed icon keeps keyboard focus. Canvas marks and dimensions are the primary relation list: hover highlights, click selects, Delete removes, double-click edits a value at its dimension and right-click opens the actions. The sketch's relations are listed under it in the feature tree, under a Relations heading that starts collapsed, mounts no row until opened, stays open once opened and opens for an explicit reveal; rows show name, operands, value and state and scroll virtually. A row selects its mark or dimension, or itself for a relation the canvas does not draw, and highlights its geometry. Shift extends one selection across marks, dimensions and rows, Delete removes the whole selection in one Undo step, and a double-click or Enter opens a row's value editor. Diagnostics reach the bar and the tree rows through one adapter, cadSketchIssuesStandInForD1, which the D1 diagnostics work replaces. Values are edited at the dimension, keeping expressions, units, parameters, reference flips, validation and pending precision. Status messages move to the top right while the bar shows. Fit keeps a sketch below the bar, and the bar is see-through and passes clicks outside its controls, so annotations under it stay visible and clickable. The relations panel, its angle sector chooser and its tests are removed; their behaviour is covered by the new components' tests.
warning: Not breaking for installed posts, machine packages, saved revisions, controller output, CAD files or agent tools. People who used the relations panel find its commands in the selection icon row, the Dimension tool, the value editor at each dimension, the feature tree's relations list and the thin bar; Fix X and Fix Y become a dimension from the H or V axis. While a sketch is open, status messages show at the top right instead of the top centre.

checklist.schema: No schema change. The sketch graph, relation kinds, CAD document and save envelope, UPID, post schema and engine API are unchanged. Saved sketches open and save byte for byte as before.
checklist.events: No execution event, input-version or cancellation change. Relation presses use the existing applySketchEdits and submitEdit path with the same native judge, draft rules and Undo steps as the panel's Apply; a refusal keeps the version and reports through the same feedback, now shown in the bar's issue list and the tree rows.
checklist.capabilities: No post or machine capability change. WebMCP tools, their arguments, results and discovery are unchanged: 49 CAD tools, 51,178 of 51,200 discovery bytes, the same as 0.0.794. The public agent guide changes only in two sentences that describe the human interface.
checklist.auditAndOutput: No generation, audit, numbering, encoding, line ending, feed or controller-file change.
checklist.installationAndStorage: No installed package, revision, browser-cache or folder storage change. Nothing is migrated or rewritten.
checklist.verification: Merged with main at 0.0.795 (#110). On the merged tree, full Vitest passes 629 files and 7,282 tests, and the production build, lint with the precision literal and feature-activity checks, ui:check, icons:check, the documentation check and check-release against origin/main pass. The icon integration audit is regenerated. WebMCP discovery is 51,178 bytes, unchanged. Relation, dimension, panel, area and sketch workflow specs pass, each run alone with two workers. Mutations caught: an icon row omitting the first available offer fails 4 tests, Delete on a selected mark doing nothing fails 22, a tree row not selecting its mark fails 2, and a diagnostic not reaching the bar fails 3. Hover over a 300-relation sketch at 4x CPU throttle, 150 pointer moves, median of 10 runs against the 0.0.794 build alternately: delay to handle a move 20.9 ms against 21.0 ms, script time 546 ms against 538 ms, style and layout time the same. Opening that sketch, median of 18 opens in three alternating rounds per build: canvas shown in 455 ms against 452.5 ms, and analysed in 485.5 ms against 477.5 ms, with no relation row mounted on either. Since review round 1. (1) Whole-edge Fix is withdrawn. Fix holds points only, as in 0.0.794, because fixing every defining point of a line or arc over-defines the sketch whenever another relation already holds part of that edge; a rank-checked edge Fix moves to S4b. (2) Pressing an icon keeps keyboard focus: while the edit applies, the row stays with aria-busy and aria-disabled buttons, and afterwards focus stays on the pressed icon, moves to the nearest usable one, or returns to the canvas. (3) Deleting the focused tree row moves focus and the tab stop to the nearest surviving row, or to the heading when none is left. (4) Drawn marks and dimensions and the listed rows of undrawn relations are one selection that Shift extends either way, with Show relations off and past the 200-mark limit; Delete or the menu removes it in one edit and one Undo step. (5) The icon row is tested against the selection's drawn geometry and never covers it; with no clear place it hides and the status line points to Constrain and Dimension. (6) Fit treats the bar as an occlusion, including the 3D fit while dependent areas are chosen. The bar yields: it is see-through, passes clicks outside its controls and turns opaque on hover or focus. The value editor keeps clear of the dock and the bar. (7) The tree's relations list starts collapsed, mounts no row until opened, stays open, and opens for an explicit reveal; open time is at parity with 0.0.794. (8) The public CAD guide describes canvas marks, the icon row and the tree list instead of a relation panel. Since review round 2. (1) One list now builds the icon row, the Constrain menu's For the selection section, the selection's right-click relations and the Dimension tool's relation items, with the same names, enabled, blocked and applied states, reasons and removal, so the no-room message holds by construction. A line and an axis read Collinear, a point and a curve Point on curve, two circles with a line also offer Symmetric centers, and four or more elements get the relations that fit them. The relation registry gained the two centre choices only the old menu offered: an arc or circle with the origin (Concentric) or with an axis (Coincident). A workbench test compares the row and the menu for 14 selections and the edits from pressing five relations in each. (2) The value editor at a dimension stays between the bar and the dock whether it opens below or above its label, and when it is taller than the room between them it starts under the bar and scrolls; a test covers the bar edge, the dock edge and the scrolling case. Full Vitest passes 629 files and 7,286 tests; the production build, lint, ui:check, icons:check, the documentation check and check-release alone and against origin/main pass; the constraint, relation mark, selectable axes, symmetry and dimension specs touched pass, each run alone with two workers.

publicNotes.summary: Sketch editing uses canvas marks, a selection icon row and a thin bar across the top.
changes: While a sketch is open, a thin bar across the top shows its name and status, a count of constraint issues that lists them, the Show dimensions and Show relations toggles, Finish and, for a sketch a solid uses, Cancel sketch edits.

Select points and edges to see a row of relation icons beside them, never over the selection and, where it can, clear of dimension labels and marks. When there is no room the row stays hidden. The Constrain menu always lists the same relations, by the same names, under For the selection, and right-click and the Dimension tool offer them too. Press an icon to add its relation, or a pressed icon to remove it. An icon that cannot apply is disabled and says why, and Dimension the selection starts a dimension on the picks.
Two circles with a line or an axis offer Symmetric centers beside Symmetric, which mirrors only their centers so each radius keeps its own dimension.

Relation marks and dimensions on the canvas act as the relation list: hover highlights, click selects, Delete removes, double-click edits a value where the dimension is drawn, and right-click opens the actions.

The sketch's relations are listed under it in the feature tree, behind a Relations heading that starts collapsed and opens when you reveal a relation. A row selects its mark, Shift adds to the selection, Delete removes everything selected in one undo step, and long lists scroll smoothly.
To hold one coordinate of a point, dimension it from the H or V axis.
Fit keeps a sketch below the bar, and dimensions and marks under the bar stay visible and clickable.
A dimension's value editor stays between the bar and the tool dock, and scrolls when they leave it too little room.
Status messages show at the top right while a sketch is open, so they never cover the bar.
publicNotes.compatibility: Installed machine packages, posts, saved revisions, controller output, CAD files and agent tools are unchanged.
